title: N-able N-central 4EverAble2Shell (Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 chain): 21 servers compromised with XMRig, 19 on patched HF2; no fix
why: Huntback found 21 N-central servers mining Monero via the 4EverAble2Shell chain on Nov 12, 19 of them on the Nov 10 HF2 build. Previdian saw full exploit-chain attempts on its honeypot from 08:30 UTC. N-able says it has seen no compromise, turned off Legacy API and Intune on hosted instances, and has no fix yet. The chain's Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance for the Agent2Shell SYSTEM chain on Windows agents.
action: Confirm Legacy API is disabled on on-prem N-central and block /dms/services/ServerUI from the internet. Hunt for an xvd.service unit, miners, or /tmp/.xvd and /var/tmp/.xvd, and treat any hit as a full server compromise.
product: N-central on-premises 2026.4 HF2 (build 2026.4.1.26) and earlier; 4EverAble2Shell requires the non-default Legacy API to be enabled and reachable

title: Check Point Gaia DynamicCLI root privilege escalation (CVE-2026-123039) exploited with PHP2Shell against Security Gateways
why: Check Point Research confirms attackers used PHP2Shell on Mobile Access portals from Oct 30, then CVE-2026-123039 to get root. About two dozen gateways were compromised, with webshells, the TSGA backdoor, an ESXi pivot and a wiper at some Israeli victims. PHP2Shell is in KEV, but CVE-2026-123039 is not in CISA KEV (Senserva 7-day KEV list, Nov 12).
action: Install the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Check Point gateways and management servers, internet-facing Mobile Access gateways first. Check Mobile Access template directories for unexpected zz*.tpl files.
product: Check Point Quantum Security Gateway / Gaia OS with Mobile Access (fixed in November Jumbo Hotfix; R82.20 Take 14)

title: ScreenConnect RMM+ extension default/blank API secret (CVE-2026-127063) abused to push rogue clients and SCKit to managed endpoints
why: ConnectWise (as CNA) assigned CVE-2026-127063 on Nov 12 to the RMM+ extension's default static API secret. Huntress links the Nov 11 SCKit incident (288 endpoints, 48 orgs, commands with no matching logins) to RMM+ 1.0.31/1.0.32 accepting a blank key. ConnectWise disabled RMM+ in about 400 partner environments. No fixed RMM+ version exists. CVE-2026-127063 is not in CISA KEV (the earlier KEV entry CVE-2026-84869 covers only the client spread step), and there is no Microsoft guidance.
action: On on-prem ScreenConnect, disable and uninstall RMM+ and related extensions now. Review Run Command and Toolbox history since Nov 11 for mass commands or ScreenConnect installer downloads. Make sure technician clients are on 26.6.5 or later.
product: DataComm RMM+ third-party extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect (Huntress: 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accept a blank key); no fixed version announced

title: Xen Orchestra VSA-2026-062: vendor-confirmed exploited auth bypass to admin and XCP-ng root takeover (no CVE yet)
why: Vates' advisory VSA-2026-062 (Nov 10) says the flaw is actively exploited by a named threat actor; BleepingComputer, THN and SC Media report it. No CVE assigned, so nothing in CISA KEV. Ostorlab and Rescana confirmed on Nov 11: still no CVE and not in KEV.
action: Update to Xen Orchestra 6.9.2 / 6.10.1 (xo-server 5.211.2 / 5.213.1), take XO off the internet, check for the pivot2 VM and hvm_serial:file configs listed in VSA-2026-062, and rotate all secrets.
product: Xen Orchestra / XOA before 6.9.2 (stable) / 6.10.1 (latest); xo-server before 5.211.2 / 5.213.1

title: Turla 'Cereal' toolset hides in Microsoft Exchange transport pipeline to steal government NATO/EU email
why: ESET published (Nov 10) a new Turla toolset found on government Exchange servers in Kazakhstan and Romania that injects into EdgeTransport.exe and uses the Exchange server itself as C2; IOCs are on ESET's GitHub. There is no CVE, KEV entry or Microsoft guidance on Cereal in the sources seen, and the initial-access vector is unknown.
action: Hunt on on-prem Exchange servers for foreign modules loaded in EdgeTransport.exe, unexpected files in the .NET native image cache and encrypted requests to /owa/sdds/ or /autodiscover/proxyservice/, using ESET's published IOCs.
product: Microsoft Exchange Server (on-premises; affected builds not disclosed)

title: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts push a CI secret stealer; secrets taken from 1,800+ repos, with AWS and Entra ID persistence
why: Aikido, OX Security, SafeDep and StepSecurity report a live campaign since Nov 10: stolen tokens for 4,837 GitHub accounts opened ~62-66k probe PRs and the stealer ran in at least 1,806 repositories, still ongoing on Nov 12 with exfil moved to Telegram. The payload adds wfx-ci-* federated credentials to Entra ID apps and rewrites AWS role trust policies, which survive secret rotation. There is no CVE (no product bug), so no CISA KEV entry, and no Microsoft or GitHub guidance appeared in the sources reviewed.
action: Search your GitHub org for PRs titled "docs: dependency audit notes" or wfx-docs branches since Nov 10; for any hit revoke that account's tokens and rotate every secret its workflows could reach, then hunt Entra ID for federated credentials named wfx-ci-* and AWS sessions named wfx-*.
vendor: GitHub (abuse of stolen developer tokens; no product flaw)
product: GitHub Actions workflows and npm postinstall hooks in any repository a compromised account can write to (since Nov 10, 2026)

title: LNbits Lightning wallet servers: unpatched exploit used to drain funds; project tells all operators to shut down
why: On Nov 8 the LNbits project said a 'wave of attacks' had hit its servers and told every operator to shut down. One operator (BitTipBot) lost 2,285,545 sats to newly created accounts between 09:22 and 14:00 UTC (THN, CoinInsider, news.bitcoin.com). There is no CVE, no fixed release (GitHub still showed v1.6.2 at 14:46 UTC Nov 9) and no CISA KEV entry.
action: Keep every LNbits instance stopped until the project releases the fixed version. Then check for unexpected new accounts and withdrawals since Nov 8, and rotate the funding-source (LND/CLN) credentials LNbits holds.
product: LNbits (self-hosted Lightning wallet/accounts server) up to v1.6.2, the latest release; Paywall extension flagged first

title: Web3Auth (Consensys) embedded-wallet flaw exposed Keplr social-login private keys; attacker drained wallets
why: Web3Auth and Keplr confirmed a flaw in Web3Auth's infrastructure that exposed private keys of social-login wallets, and that an 'original attacker' used it from Nov 6 (The Block, THN). GoPlus estimates at least $1M stolen. The flaw is in a hosted service: there is no CVE, no public technical detail and no CISA KEV entry.
action: If you or your app use Web3Auth embedded wallets or Keplr social login, stop sending funds to those addresses. Move liquid assets to a seed-phrase or hardware wallet, and follow only official Keplr/Web3Auth channels for recovery: scam 'recovery' offers are circulating.
product: Web3Auth embedded wallet service; Keplr wallets created with Google or Apple login

title: German web host mittwald breached via its MCP (AI-assistant) server: session tokens stolen, 56 customer projects compromised
why: mittwald disclosed (blog post Nov 7, The Record) that an attacker used a flaw in its MCP server from Oct 27 to Nov 4 to read customers' session tokens and compromise 56 projects. The flaw is in a hosted service: there is no CVE, no technical writeup yet (promised for next week) and no CISA KEV entry.
action: If you are a mittwald customer who used the MCP server after Oct 27, change passwords, enable 2FA, and delete unknown API and SSH keys. Rotate the database, mail and third-party credentials stored in your projects.
product: mittwald mStudio MCP server (AI assistant interface)

title: MongoDB Server pre-auth use-after-free in replication catch-up (9.5); public PoC on GitHub
why: A GitHub PoC (indexed by Sploitus Nov 11) reproduces the unauthenticated use-after-free as a crash/memory corruption against 8.0.34; MongoDB says it knows of no exploitation. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade replica-set MongoDB servers to the fixed release for your branch and make sure mongod ports are not reachable from untrusted networks.
product: MongoDB Server replica-set members (incl. shard/config servers) before 9.0.7 / 8.3.16 / 8.0.37 / 7.0.48 / 6.0.30 / 5.0.35 / 4.4.32; standalone mongod not affected

title: SignDrop: unpatched Windows CLFS authentication zero-day, public PoC gives SYSTEM (no CVE, no MSRC advisory)
why: Nightmare Eclipse (MSNightmare) published a working PoC on Nov 10 that turns a standard user into SYSTEM by abusing CLFS authentication signing and coercing Defender. As of Nov 11 there was no CVE, no MSRC advisory or fix, and no CISA KEV entry. No in-the-wild use has been reported yet, but the same researcher's earlier drops were later abused.
action: Do not set CLFS Authentication Mode to 2 (disabled). Alert on .cnpf/.blf files created by MsMpEng.exe or other SYSTEM processes outside normal CLFS paths, and on ERROR_LOG_METADATA_CORRUPT errors, until Microsoft ships a fix.
product: Windows CLFS driver (clfs.sys) with CLFS authentication in learning or enforcement mode; tested on Windows 11 26H2 and Windows Server 2025

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6460 type confusion: low-privileged database user to OS code execution, RCE technique now public
why: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a write-up turning the 22-year-old type confusion into code execution, and an independent researcher reproduced the crash with four SQL statements as a zero-privilege role (dev.to); the item hit Hacker News today. OffSeq and SecurityOnline report no exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Hosted PostgreSQL services may be exposed, but no cloud-provider statement was found.
action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 (14 is now end-of-life), prioritising multi-tenant servers, and until then remove CREATE privileges from untrusted roles.
product: PostgreSQL before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 (part of a 52-CVE release on Nov 12, 2026)

title: hyperglass looking glass: unauthenticated command injection in /api/query; 36 ISP/hosting hosts shown exploitable, upstream unpatched
why: Disclosed Nov 10 on oss-security and hyperpwn.xyz (research attributed to DeepSeek, validated by the poster): target strings are put into router/shell commands unescaped, and /api/query is unauthenticated by default. The write-up reports 36 internet-exposed instances across 20 ASNs with command execution (11 root or equivalent). Upstream issue open since July, no CVE, not in KEV.
action: Take internet-facing hyperglass instances offline or put them behind authentication/an allowlist, and restrict query types until a fixed release exists; rotate router/SSH credentials configured in hyperglass.
product: hyperglass upstream (fix PR #382 / issue #383 still open); hardened fork z23/hyperglass mitigates

title: SGLang inference-engine RCE exploited to breach NEAR AI (no CVE, versions or upstream fix named)
why: NEAR AI's Nov 9 incident report says an attacker exploited an SGLang RCE on Nov 8 to run code on an inference server and pivot internally; it reported the bug to SGLang. No CVE, affected versions or upstream fix have been named, and nothing is in CISA KEV.
action: Keep SGLang servers off the internet behind authenticated proxies, watch the SGLang repository for a security release, and rotate any secrets reachable from inference hosts.
product: SGLang (open-source LLM inference engine); affected versions not disclosed

title: Apify breach (Nov 9-10): attacker accessed internal systems; customer billing data and 2FA recovery codes exposed, all API tokens rotated
why: Apify's status page confirms an unauthorized third party accessed internal systems on Nov 9-10, detected Nov 11. Customer notices report exposed emails, billing details and 2FA recovery codes, and some GitHub OAuth connections were revoked. There is no CVE, so nothing is in KEV, and no Microsoft coverage was seen.
action: Replace Apify API tokens in every pipeline, set up 2FA again, review GitHub activity for any account linked to Apify, and warn finance about invoice phishing that uses real billing details.
product: Apify platform (hosted)

title: Qubole's trusted AWS cross-account access abused to steal secrets, Entra ID/Okta client credentials and S3 data from customers
why: Wiz (with Sentra and Mandiant) published on Nov 9 that an attacker used Qubole-side IAM credentials Oct 14-26 to assume customer integration roles, harvest Lambda/Secrets Manager/SSM secrets (incl. Microsoft Entra ID client secrets) and copy S3 data. No vendor statement, no CVE, not in KEV, and no Microsoft advisory on the stolen Entra secrets.
action: Hunt CloudTrail from Oct 1 for AssumeRole from Qubole's AWS account originating outside AWS (per Wiz's guidance), delete unused Qubole roles, and rotate every secret, Entra ID app secret and Okta credential those roles could read.
product: Qubole data lake platform AWS integration roles (incl. dormant roles still trusting account 805246085872)

title: Malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases steal Swarm wallet keys and install backdoors
why: Ethersphere confirmed both releases were published by an attacker using its release identity/CI credentials on Nov 9 (GHSA-hh7j-5m3j-23pf / MAL-2026-18773). Socket, StepSecurity and SafeDep analysed the loader: wallet theft plus a backdoor (hidden ScreenConnect on Windows), C2 shared with the SleepyDuck campaign. No CVE, not in KEV.
action: Search lockfiles, caches and CI logs for @ethersphere/bee-js@13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2; pin bee-js 13.2.0 / install Desktop 0.56.3, rebuild any host that ran them and move Swarm node funds to a new key.
product: @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 (npm, live ~75 min Nov 9) and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 (GitHub/auto-update, ~8.5 h)

title: SAP November Patch Day: ICM2SHELL and PROXYGATE unauthenticated RCE plus SAML2 auth bypass, all CVSS 10.0
why: SAP fixed four CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated flaws on Nov 10; Onapsis named ICM2SHELL (CVE-2026-76964/89126, crafted WebSocket fragments -> RCE as <sid>adm) and PROXYGATE (CVE-2026-89103, open prxyinfo ACL -> OS commands) and says it built a working exploit (not public). No in-the-wild use reported and none are in CISA KEV.
action: Apply the November SAP Security Notes to internet-facing Web Dispatcher and ICM first, then Gateway (and lock down the prxyinfo ACL) and SAML2-enabled ABAP systems.
product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP (ICM, SAML2 SP), SAP Web Dispatcher, SAP Gateway / SAP Kernel (releases per SAP Security Notes, incl. out-of-maintenance kernels)

title: Fortinet FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer pre-auth RCE: FGFM (126261), JSON-RPC API (126170), OFTP SQLi (126262)
why: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-275/219/276 on Nov 10. FGFM and OFTP flaws are unauthenticated, and the JSON-RPC injection (126170, CVSS 9.8) gives unauthenticated code execution when the API is enabled. Fortinet says none are known exploited and none are in CISA KEV. A Sploitus 'PoC' listing is unverified. Earlier FGFM bugs (FortiJump) were mass-exploited.
action: Upgrade FortiManager to 8.0.1/7.6.8/7.4.6/7.2.9 (and FAZ per FG-IR-26-276), set 'rpc-permit none' on admin profiles if JSON API is not needed, and restrict FGFM/OFTP to known FortiGate addresses.
product: FortiManager 8.0.0, 7.6.0-7.6.7, 7.4.0-7.4.5, 7.2.0-7.2.8 (FGFM); FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer with JSON API enabled (126170) or FAZ features/OFTP (126262)

title: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-119618): Red Hat cites a reliable exploit in public research, Wiz says no exploit yet
why: Red Hat's CVE page says 'public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit' against a default mod_http2 server but does not name it. Wiz says no exploit is available and no attacks are reported. A Sploitus-indexed lab repo only shows sanitizer-level reproduction. Not in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade to httpd 2.4.71 or the distro-patched mod_http2. Until then, remove h2/h2c from the Protocols directive on internet-facing servers.
product: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled; standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 through 2.0.42

title: Fortinet FortiOS November batch: unauthenticated super-admin command execution via HA packets (126259) plus OSPF/BGP routing flaws
why: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-273 on Nov 10 (CVSS 9.8 per NVD). Its HA virtual patch is labelled '0day', and its own scores mark some bugs as having exploit code. Fortinet reports no attacks, there is no public PoC, and none of the batch is in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade FortiOS to 8.0.1, or to 7.6.8/7.4.13/7.2.14 when they ship. Until then, apply the FortiGuard HA virtual patch and keep HA/FGSP sync traffic on a dedicated non-routed segment.
product: FortiOS 8.0.0, 7.6.0-7.6.7, 7.4.0-7.4.12, 7.2.0-7.2.13 (HA FGSP with standalone-config-sync, or autoscale)

title: Fortinet FortiMail unauthenticated RCE: path traversal (126147), HA join-request command injection (126148), SMTP format string (126163)
why: Fortinet advisories FG-IR-26-199/200 (Nov 10, CVSS 9.8) list these as unauthenticated code execution and 'Known Exploited: No'. Rescana confirmed they were not in CISA KEV on Nov 11. A GitHub 'PoC' for 126147 indexed on Sploitus is only a simulated lab, not a working exploit against FortiMail.
action: Upgrade FortiMail to 8.0.2/7.6.7/7.4.9 (migrate off 7.2), and restrict the management interface and HA ports to trusted networks.

title: Synology DSM pre-auth SQL injection in Auth API (9.8) and rsync auth bypass allow unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write
why: Synology SA-26:19 (Nov 10, CVE published Nov 12) fixes an unauthenticated SQL injection with arbitrary file write. Viettel, who reported it, calls it a pre-auth zero-click RCE. No exploitation or public PoC yet and not in CISA KEV, while Synology NAS devices are already being hit by ransomware via an older DSM flaw.
action: Update DSM to 7.2.1-69057-13 / 7.2.2-72806-10 / 7.3.2-86009-5 / 7.4.1-90080-1 or later, and keep DSM (ports 5000/5001) and rsync off the internet.

title: Fireworks AI second breach via its cloud provider exposes customer data incl. Notion AI chat transcripts
why: Fireworks notified customers Nov 9 (Bloomberg, BleepingComputer) that an attacker pivoted from a breached third-party cloud provider to its development machines on Oct 24, touching tens of thousands of files with some customer data. Notion's advisory says Notion AI chat transcripts from fewer than 1% of workspaces were exposed. No CVE, not in KEV.
action: If you use Fireworks or Notion AI, check for breach notifications and rotate any credentials or API keys that were pasted into Notion AI or stored in Fireworks jobs since October.
product: Fireworks AI inference/fine-tuning platform (development machines); downstream Notion (<1% of workspaces), Cursor and others

title: iOS 'worse_query' sandbox escape PoC lets a malicious app read other apps' files; no Apple fix confirmed
why: Researcher forcequitOS published a developer PoC on GitHub Nov 8 and Binance warned users Nov 10; Apple's iOS 27.2.1/26.7.3 notes (Nov 9) do not mention it and no fix is confirmed. No exploitation or thefts reported; no CVE, not in KEV.
action: Update managed iPhones/iPads to iOS 27.2.1 or 26.7.3, block sideloaded/enterprise-signed apps via MDM, and tell users not to keep secrets in plaintext on the device.
product: Apple iOS 26.0-26.7.2 and 27.2 per researcher (Binance lists 26.7.1, 27.0.1, 27.2); unclear whether iOS 27.2.1 / 26.7.3 fix it

title: Ivanti Endpoint Manager unauthenticated SQL injection to RCE (9.8) and Cloud Services Application missing auth (9.4)
why: Ivanti's November EPM advisory and NVD (Nov 10) describe a remote unauthenticated SQL injection in the EPM Core leading to code execution; no exploitation or public PoC reported, not in CISA KEV. Ivanti EPM bugs have been targeted after past disclosures.
action: Upgrade EPM Core to 2024 SU8, update the Cloud Services Application past 5.0.8, and keep the EPM Core and CSA consoles off the internet.
product: Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8; Ivanti Cloud Services Application 5.0.8

title: React Server Components unauthenticated RCE in rare typed-array cases (react-server-dom-*)
why: React published GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3 / CVE-2026-126187 on Nov 10 (CVSS 9.5). No public PoC or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. The prior RSC bug (React2Shell, CVE-2025-55182) went to mass exploitation.
action: Upgrade react-server-dom-webpack/parcel/turbopack to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 (and the framework release that pins them).

title: Git recursive-clone RCE via index path truncation (plus five more Git fixes)
why: Git and GitHub disclosed the fixes on Nov 10; no public exploit or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. No MSRC advisory seen for Git bundled in Microsoft developer tools.
action: Update Git everywhere (workstations, CI runners, bundled copies) to a fixed release and avoid recursive clones of untrusted repositories meanwhile.

title: AntiFox AI pentest platform (ARTEX fork) used to breach IIS web servers and steal AWS production secrets
why: Arctic Wolf Labs (Nov 11, covered by BleepingComputer and THN) tied AntiFox instances hosted on Alibaba Cloud to confirmed intrusions: IIS webshells, then a successful GetSecretValue on a production secret and S3 copy/delete. The IIS entry vulnerability is unknown and there's no CVE, so nothing for KEV. Microsoft has written about ARTEX, the parent framework, but not about AntiFox.
action: Hunt IIS hosts for new ASPX webshells. Rotate any AWS keys stored in web.config or logs. Alert on GetSecretValue and bursts of AccessDenied from new source infrastructure, and enforce IMDSv2.
product: Internet-facing IIS web applications and the AWS accounts behind them (abuse campaign, no product CVE)

title: Citrix NetScaler November fixes: Console unauth bypass (CVE-2026-120869, 9.4) and default-config ADC/Gateway memory overflow (CVE-2026-120868, 9.3)
why: Citrix bulletins (Nov 11-12) fix an unauthenticated Console auth bypass and a packet-processing overflow that affects every ADC/Gateway, default config included. watchTowr is building exposure checks. Citrix reports no exploitation, no confirmed public PoC exists, and none of these CVEs is in CISA KEV.
action: Upgrade internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39 and NetScaler Console to 14.1-74.34. Until then, restrict Console access to management hosts.
product: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.57, 13.1 before 13.1-64.39; NetScaler Console before 14.1-74.34

title: Red Hat Quay unauthenticated signing-key takeover (CVE-2026-123710, 9.8) plus cross-tenant robot-token theft (CVE-2026-110697); no fixed release named
why: Red Hat disclosed the bug on Nov 11. An anonymous /v2/auth token can authorize service-key rotation, letting an attacker install a non-expiring signing key and forge tokens for every repository. Upstream fixes were merged Nov 11, but no fixed release was named as of reporting. There is no PoC or ITW report, and it is not in CISA KEV.
action: Block /keys at the proxy so only trusted internal components can reach it. Review service_key_rotate audit events for keys with no expiration and remove any you don't recognize.
product: Red Hat Quay 3 and Quay 5 (standalone, Quay Operator on OpenShift, mirror registry for OpenShift); exposed when /keys is reachable by untrusted clients

title: WorkOS breach: researcher's ARTEX AI agent used a leaked dev credential to pull customer CRM/support data
why: WorkOS's Nov 6 bulletin update (BleepingComputer, Nov 6) says an ARTEX agent run by a researcher reached an internet-exposed internal API with a predictable dev credential (Oct 25-30) and extracted customer records. This is an incident at a SaaS vendor, so there is no CVE, KEV entry or Microsoft advisory to cover it.
action: If you are a WorkOS customer, warn staff about phishing that cites real WorkOS support or sales conversations. Audit your own internal tools for internet exposure and leftover dev credentials.
product: WorkOS internal sales/customer-support tool (not the WorkOS auth product)

title: Firefox 160 / ESR 153.7 / ESR 115.45 fix 70+ memory-safety bugs incl. seven 9.6 sandbox escapes
why: NVD published the Firefox 160 batch on Nov 10 with seven CVSS 9.6 sandbox escapes and dozens of 8.8 use-after-free bugs; none is reported exploited and none is in KEV.
action: Roll Firefox to 160 and ESR to 153.7 / 115.45 across managed desktops.
product: Firefox before 160, Firefox ESR before 153.7 and before 115.45

title: Node.js November 2026 security release: 16 CVEs incl. HTTPS cross-connection memory leak exposing TLS private keys (CVE-2026-123864)
why: Node.js shipped 16 fixes on Nov 11, seven rated High. CVE-2026-123864 lets an unauthenticated client read other connections' memory, including TLS private keys, and several HTTP/2 bugs let a client crash default servers. No exploitation or public PoC reported, and none are in KEV.
action: Upgrade to Node.js 22.23.5/24.22.3/26.13.1, rebuild container images, and consider rotating TLS keys on HTTPS services that ran affected handlers.
product: Node.js 22.x before 22.23.5, 24.x before 24.22.3, 26.x before 26.13.1 (end-of-life lines always affected)

title: Zoom Workplace for Windows critical privilege escalation over the network (CVE-2026-108186, 9.6) and origin validation flaw (108187)
why: Zoom bulletins ZSB-26023/24 (Nov 10) rate 108186 Critical 9.6 with user interaction required. No exploitation or public PoC and not in CISA KEV. This is a Windows app but not a Microsoft product, so no MSRC advisory applies.
action: Push Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.8 or later to all endpoints, including per-user installs that bypass central deployment.
product: Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.0 before 7.1.8 (108186); before 7.1.5 (108187)

title: IBM Concert 1.0-3.0.1.1 unauthenticated OS command injection (CVE-2026-6715, CVE-2026-15266, CVSS 9.8)
why: IBM published two CVSS 9.8 (AV:N/PR:N) OS command injection CVEs, which NVD listed on Nov 8 (IBM advisory node 7294607). VulDB says no public exploit. Neither CVE is in CISA KEV.
action: Apply the fix in IBM advisory 7294607 and restrict network access to the Concert UI and API to admin networks.
product: IBM Concert 1.0 through 3.0.1.1

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO (EOL) batch: pre-auth root command injection and hardcoded backdoor password (CVE-2026-124002..124015)
why: VulnCheck published a batch of 14 XWEB EVO CVEs on Nov 12, including unauthenticated root command injection (CVSS 9.8) and a hardcoded admin backdoor password. This comes while the sibling XWEB PRO (CVE-2026-25085) is being exploited in refrigeration sabotage. There is no public exploit and no reported in-the-wild use, and none of the CVEs is in CISA KEV.
action: Take XWEB EVO web interfaces off the internet now, put them behind VPN or allowlists, and plan to replace these end-of-service units.
product: XWEB EVO refrigeration/HVAC supervisor, 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 depending on CVE; product line end of service March 2026
